title: Governance in social-ecological agent-based models: a review

key_points.claim: Many social-ecological ABMs lack explicit theoretical grounding for governance and actor decision-making.
key_points.evidence_quote: a significant share of the literature is not explicitly based on theories supporting the modeling of governance and actors’ decision making

key_points.claim: State intervention dominates modeled governance modes; community- and market-based modes and formal/informal institutions are rare.
key_points.evidence_quote: The governance modes that are mostly modeled are state interventions whereas the community-based and market-based modes of governance are scarcely represented.

key_points.claim: Theoretical background is mostly neoclassical economics; command-and-control and economic instruments are the most common policy instruments.
key_points.evidence_quote: A little less than two-thirds of these models are grounded in neoclassical economics

key_points.claim: Two implementation forms exist: governance as a variable (preferred) versus governance as an agent. Agent-based governance models rely more on institutional theories, represent information instruments and have more interactions.
key_points.evidence_quote: In terms of implementation, governance as a variable is preferred to that as an agent.

key_points.claim: Bidirectional governance-SES links are uncommon; governance mostly acts on ecology through actors' decisions.
key_points.evidence_quote: Bidirectional links are found in approximately one-fifth of all models.

key_points.claim: ABMs have mostly been used to compare theories, examine case studies and predict; rarely to develop new theory.
key_points.evidence_quote: rarely to develop a new theory for analyzing SES

key_points.claim: Limitations of ABM: parameter proliferation, lack of transparency, models either highly conceptual or case-specific.
key_points.evidence_quote: the number of parameters can be high and the model difficult to calculate

key_points.claim: Recommendation: greater diversity in governance representation, better model dynamics, explicit theory use and governance represented as an agent.
key_points.evidence_quote: representation of governance as an agent

reliability_notes: Full text fetched (peer-reviewed, open access, 2021). Only abstract, introduction and discussion were read; methods and results details (e.g., number of reviewed articles) were not extracted. It covers social-ecological ABMs rather than general artificial societies.
